meta.title: Gamble Battle RGA + Trait Matrix
meta.proofModel: zero-sum 9-archetype tournament with deterministic bridge feasibility

traits.strategicJob: Reactive anti-burst shell that turns repeated casts into timed defensive leverage.
Spell-power vertical whose kill stacks and capstone casting reward protected timing windows.
Healing and shielding vertical that turns controlled overheal into a visible safety buffer.
Short-window control answer: tenacity first, then a readable cleanse-and-shield breakpoint.
Turns a deliberately mixed cost curve into team value without demanding a vertical board.
Long-horizon item-combination engine that trades immediate board power for future flexibility.
Attack-speed tempo lever that accelerates an allied clock while taxing the opposing clock.
Converts a first successful threshold kill into escalating crit, bleed, and shield-bypass pressure.
Exact-count puzzle that rewards stopping at a chosen breakpoint instead of mindless vertical stacking.
Broad damage-reduction vertical that buys time but remains bypassable, shreddable, and clockable.
Wide-board constraint that pays only when the largest trait stays intentionally small.
Rewards distinct active traits, turning breadth into medium-strength distributed threats.
Formation-link vertical that makes adjacency and triangle geometry a pre-combat decision.
Pupil engine that makes one carry exceptional while exposing a clear source and target.
Mana-cost and full-cast volatility vertical that compresses caster timing windows.
Omnivamp and overheal funnel that wins medium-pressure fights but exposes threshold risk.
Reliable mana regeneration that creates a readable cast-count clock rather than raw stats.
Attack-damage kill-stacking vertical that needs uptime and a first takedown to snowball.
Maximum-health and cast-stacking vertical that anchors long fights without protecting the backline for free.
Reroll economy vertical that buys scouting flexibility at the cost of immediate committed power.
Armor and resistance shred that gives range and uptime boards a deliberate anti-fortress answer.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 01
bridgeUnits.hook: Overheal becomes a short team bulwark after this unit absorbs a threshold of damage.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 02
bridgeUnits.hook: Basic attacks bank healing; the bank detonates as a self-risking frontline pulse.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 03
bridgeUnits.hook: Long shots fortify the most threatened ally instead of only increasing damage.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 04
bridgeUnits.hook: Marks one threat; blocking its cast shreds its defenses for the team.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 05
bridgeUnits.hook: Dodges one committed cast, then leaves a temporary resistance wound on the caster.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 06
bridgeUnits.hook: Repeated shots alternate a personal ward with stacking armor and resistance fracture.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 07
bridgeUnits.hook: Stores allied spell casts, then releases a modest burst whose shape depends on the last caster.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 08
bridgeUnits.hook: Creates a focus zone where the next allied cast is safer but visibly telegraphed.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 09
bridgeUnits.hook: Each uninterrupted attack improves the next shop rebate, but changing targets clears the streak.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 10
bridgeUnits.hook: Accurate volleys build a temporary discount token; missed uptime resets both damage and value.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 11
bridgeUnits.hook: A threshold kill grants one reposition and converts the victim's tier into a reroll fragment.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 12
bridgeUnits.hook: Selects a contracted ally to enter first; success amplifies, failure taxes the next cast.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 13
bridgeUnits.hook: Redirects one projectile while warded, then loses the ward until it absorbs enough damage.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 14
bridgeUnits.hook: Crosses the line under a brittle ward that breaks into a brief silence instead of more damage.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 15
bridgeUnits.hook: A protected channel paints a damage clock; losing the shield ends the clock early.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 16
bridgeUnits.hook: Fires through a fortified firing lane; enemies can step aside or break the lane source.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 17
bridgeUnits.hook: Telegraphs one distant verdict; the cast is lethal only if earlier spell pressure set the threshold.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 18
bridgeUnits.hook: Spends stored spell power to blink once; a failed execute leaves it exposed with no second jump.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 19
bridgeUnits.hook: Body-checks the densest frontline; the impact scales with health lost, not maximum health alone.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 20
bridgeUnits.hook: Gains heavier ammunition as the target survives, creating a visible anti-health clock.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 21
bridgeUnits.hook: Ignores the first control event only while escaping; using it offensively removes the exit route.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 22
bridgeUnits.hook: Links a pupil across a lane and redirects one threat through the link's visible geometry.

bridgeUnits.label: Temporary Unit 23
bridgeUnits.hook: Spends mana as health to seed a damage-over-time clock, then heals only if the clock completes.

archetypes.name: Bastion Siege
archetypes.plan: Layer fortification, peel, and redirect around sustained carries.
archetypes.failureMode: Clumped protection becomes a target for zones and synchronized detonation.

archetypes.name: Dive Reset
archetypes.plan: Breach the backline, secure the first threshold kill, and chain resets.
archetypes.failureMode: If the first kill is denied, the board is stranded in hostile space.

archetypes.name: Zone Control
archetypes.plan: Turn board geometry into damage, pathing tax, and split timing.
archetypes.failureMode: Long-range source kill or mobile threats can ignore the intended path.

archetypes.name: Attrition Engine
archetypes.plan: Survive the first wave and win through sustain, ramp, and attack uptime.
archetypes.failureMode: Execute, anti-heal, shred, or denied uptime ends the engine before payback.

archetypes.name: Wombo Engage
archetypes.plan: Start one favorable fight and synchronize area burst into cleanup.
archetypes.failureMode: Spread, immunity, redirect, or mistimed entry breaks the cast chain.

archetypes.name: Control Prison
archetypes.plan: Delay the enemy's key plan long enough for focused follow-up to decide the fight.
archetypes.failureMode: Cleanse, immunity, untargetable timing, or damage clocks make delay worthless.

archetypes.name: Wide Trait Engine
archetypes.plan: Use many medium threats and linked traits so no single counter solves the board.
archetypes.failureMode: AoE, formation breaking, and source pressure collapse distributed value.

archetypes.name: Long-Range Siege
archetypes.plan: Win lanes from distance and delete the opposing engine before contact.
archetypes.failureMode: Hard engage, dive, and broken firing lines erase range advantage.

archetypes.name: Anti-Meta Flex
archetypes.plan: Scout, pivot, and field the exact answer to a committed opponent.
archetypes.failureMode: A wrong read leaves shallow synergies against a fully committed board.

counterEdges.reason: Redirect and peel deny the first reset kill.
Layered defense punishes a low-commitment or incorrect pivot.
Backline access removes the amplifier before distributed value stabilizes.
The firing line collapses once assassins breach it.
Hazards tax the clumped protection shell and route around its anchor.
Dangerous paths split engage timing before the detonation window.
Delay without enough damage feeds the sustain-and-ramp clock.
A committed engine outscales shallow counter pieces.
The protected clump supplies the ideal synchronized burst target.
Hard engage closes distance before siege accrues enough uptime.
Lockdown denies the first takedown and therefore the reset chain.
Disabling the engage source breaks the cast sequence.
Distributed threats and debuff access overload one sustain axis.
Spread formation reduces the value of each hazard cell.
Source-priority range removes exposed amp and link pieces.
Sustained shred wins before melee uptime reaches the firing line.
Source-kill and mobility pivots invalidate the chosen hazard plan.
Cleanse and immunity pivots turn the main lockdown investment off.
Peel preserves the carry long enough to race the slower engine.
Durable midline bodies can survive imperfect threshold access.
Untargetable timing can cross one hazard window, but not every lane.
Uptime denial taxes healing and ramp without directly deleting them.
If the opener is diffuse, sustain recovers before cleanup.
A clean opener can catch divers before they fan out.
Fast commitment punishes a pivot that spends too long scouting.
Spread and immunity pivots can tax one scripted engage.
Distributed threats still create enough bodies for area payoff.
Multiple damage channels stretch a single protection plan.
Cleanse timing and redundant carries reduce single-target control value.
Locking the zone source can open one safe route.
A well-placed denial lane can force the firing line off ideal tiles.
Source pressure can remove control pieces before repeated casts.
Targeting the link hub temporarily collapses part of the web.
Breadth makes one specific pivot insufficient.
A correctly scouted engage or immunity package taxes static range.
Shred and reach can pressure the anchor without entering peel range.

promisedPairs.choice: Maximum health and overheal can coexist, but only by exposing four shared bridge units.
The same bridges alternate protection and shred, creating timing rather than a pure stat wall.
Eight Arcanists and six Overload casters fit exactly, so disruption and source priority remain decisive.
Combat streaks and reroll flexibility share four fragile economic fighters instead of becoming free value.
